locator.paragraph: Immediately following the high false-positive-rate sentence quoted by Eiben et al.; example of a 20-year-old pregnant woman

correction: Rüffer’s complete speech explicitly conditions the 52 percent on a positive result, rather than treating it as a share of every test. The submission’s own later explanation of positive predictive value is compatible with that denominator. This does not establish what she or the other speakers privately understood.
effect: An allegation that the parliamentary concerns depend on confusing all tests with positive tests would be weaker for this quoted speech. Whether this is the authors’ exact allegation remains unresolved; they may principally reject the framing of rare overall false-positive outcomes as worrying.
limits: The claim uses an inference, deuten, and the later text expressly offers the authors’ judgment about whether the frequency is worrying. Concern among test-positive patients and frequency among all tested patients can coexist. The Welt article has not been independently read, so its full context is not adjudicated. No clinical test-performance, screening-appropriateness or policy conclusion follows. No intent is inferred.
context_and_alternatives: Full four-page author article and four-page exact motion read. Author welcomes monitoring rather than asking for rejection of the motion.

The author quotes two MPs and a newspaper, then explains the distinction between positive-test results and all results. Rüffer’s conditional example immediately follows the excerpt the author selected; Kappert-Gonther interjects agreement. Her own later speech explains that positive results require invasive diagnostic clarification.

The general term rate is potentially ambiguous without a denominator, but the adjacent sentence supplies it. A complaint about the rhetorical impression of the first sentence is different from a factual allegation that the speaker confused denominators.

The original Lu 2024 primary study, including its age-specific tables, supports the author’s approximate young-women positive predictive value and rarity figures. No separate numerical test-performance issue is promoted.
Lu 2024 is expressly retrospective, whereas the author calls it prospective. Prospective data collection within a retrospective analysis is a possible benign reading; no separate finding is asserted.
materiality_explanation: Potentially minor source-description issue: this is an auxiliary criticism of the premises for an evaluation which the author nevertheless expressly supports. It does not determine the proposed monitoring or committee design.
direction_explanation: Null while the interpretive issue remains unresolved. A confirmed overstatement would support the author’s request to reshape the evaluation around what they describe as the current factual position.
